application.source: classification mapping required by the facts audit brief

chemistry.source: Crawford 2026 DOE OE peer-review poster, alias table (https://doepeerreview.sandia.gov/app/uploads/sites/82/2026/05/Crawford_Alasdair_Analytics.pdf); per system in fielddata/loaders/pnnl_epri.py

units_released.note: Rule: one per system, EPRI_NMC2 left out (it is the ppl E.W. Brown system, counted once, under ppl). Released unit identifiers require package-specific inspection.

cells_liion.note: The release gives pack- or system-level signals and no cell topology.

cells_leadacid.note: No lead-acid cell count applies or is exposed in this release.

cell_channels_measured.note: No individual cell-voltage channels are released.

energy_mwh.source: PNNL reports for the six WACEF systems (ENW at its 4 MWh nameplate) and the Crawford 2026 poster for the EPRI systems; per system in reports/candidates/pnnl_epri/pnnl_epri_ratings.csv
energy_mwh.note: Nine systems: Avista 3.2, ENW 4.0, OPALCO 2.0, PSE 4.4, SnoPUDMESA1 1.0, SnoPUDMESA2 8.0, EPRI_LFP3 40.0, EPRI_NMC1 1.0, EPRI_VRF1 0.27 MWh. EPRI_LFP1 and EPRI_LFP2 are unrated, and EPRI_NMC2 is ppl's system, counted there. ENW: PNNL's 5.5 MWh designed usable is noted, the nameplate is used (maintainer, 2026-10-13). Split basis: 23.87 MWh stated (the eight other rated systems) and 40.0 MWh computed (EPRI_LFP3). EPRI_LFP3: 40 MWh computed from the data's peak power of 0.25 C, a 4-hour ratio, at the poster's 10 MW, which matches the poster's printed E/P of 4.0 (maintainer, 2026-10-16: trust the data; computed, not stated). The poster also states 30,000 kWh (3 hours); the poster's 30 MWh is noted as a discrepancy. The data are normalised, so they fix the ratio, not the absolute size: 30 MWh run at no more than 7.5 MW would also fit. EPRI_NMC1 and EPRI_VRF1 rest on the poster alone. The data are normalised by unreleased ratings, so energy is not computable from them (usable fractions in reports/checks/v12/pnnl_epri_energy.csv).

energy_basis.source: energy_mwh is 23.87 MWh stated (eight rated systems) and 40.0 MWh computed (EPRI_LFP3); totals count each part under its basis

span_unit_years.source: fielddata.loaders.pnnl_epri (first to last HoursElapsed per system, scripts/checks/pnnl_epri_units.py)
span_unit_years.note: Eleven systems, plus EPRI_NMC2's 304 days before ppl's first file (0.832 unit-years): EPRI_NMC2 is ppl's E.W. Brown system, counted once, and its time outside ppl still counts.

obs_hours.note: Observation-hours are not used when calendar spans are measurable or no cadence is available.

fault_onset_timestamp.source: docs/descriptor/TABLE3_faults.md; released labels and metadata contain no explicit fault-onset timestamp field

sentinels_documented.source: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22947521; public data record and released documentation state no sentinel convention

energy_split_computed_mwh.note: EPRI_LFP3: the data's 0.25 C peak power (a 4-hour ratio) at the poster's 10 MW

energy_split_stated_mwh.note: Avista 3.2, ENW 4.0, OPALCO 2.0, PSE 4.4, SnoPUDMESA1 1.0, SnoPUDMESA2 8.0, EPRI_NMC1 1.0, EPRI_VRF1 0.27 MWh

units_gross.note: Gross: all 12 systems, including EPRI_NMC2, which is ppl's system. Not used in totals.
